subject: Model running time and a possible issue with lognormal scale parameter

messages.subject: Model running time and a possible issue with lognormal scale parameter
parts:
Hi,

I trying to write a model of 3 purchase decisions - time (log-logistic), quantity (log-normal) and quote acceptance (logit), incorporated with a control function for price endogeneity (following Petrin&Train). 
This is a hierarchical model with multiple observations per client and the likelihood function should have the following form:
f(t)*f(q)*Pr(quote acceptance)f(p)
f(p) is added as part of the control function approach and specifically the logit utility under this approach is:
U_ij = X'beta + gamma(p - p_hat) + random normal error

The model is very slow to run. Especially after adding the control function. Below is the code for random coefficients model with correlated betas within every equation. I realize that using the LKJ transformation instead of inv wishart will make things much better, but I also tried removing the correlation between the betas, as well as a random intercept model with correlated betas, but none of them seems to perform better. 
I also tried different initial values. 

It might be related and might not, but although I define the parameter to a lognormal as follows:
sigma ~ normal(0.5, sqrt(2)); 
and then pass a positive transformation of sigma to the function:
obs_q[i,j] ~ lognormal(dot_product(x_q[i,j], beta_q[i]), sigma^2); 
or
obs_q[i,j] ~ lognormal(dot_product(x_q[i,j], beta_q[i]), exp(sigma));

In both cases I keep getting these error messages (although only at the beginning but multiple times and definitely not sporadically) .   

Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:
stan::prob::lognormal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Scale parameter is inf:0, but must be finite!
If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,
but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.

Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:
stan::prob::lognormal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Scale parameter is 0:0, but must be > 0!
If this warning occurs sporadically, such as for highly constrained variable types like covariance matrices, then the sampler is fine,
but if this warning occurs often then your model may be either severely ill-conditioned or misspecified.

Model code:
functions {

/* Eq (5) in Zhang 2014 (published) */
real log_two_logistic_logpdf(real t, real xb, real alpha) {
  real top;
  real bot;

top <- xb + log(alpha) + (alpha - 1) * log(t);
bot <- 2 * log1p(exp(xb) * t^alpha);

return top - bot;  
}
/* log of survival function */
real log_two_logistic_survival(real t, real xb, real alpha) {
real top;
real bot;

top <- exp(xb) * t^alpha ;
bot <- 1 + exp(xb) * t^alpha;

return log(1 - top/bot);  
}
}

cov_matrix[dim_q] inv_V_q0;

real<lower=0>     mu_lambda_sd;

// Prior covariances

real<lower=1> df_q0;
real<lower=1> df_w0;

cov_matrix[dim_q] S_q0;

real<lower=0>     sig_lambda_sd;

/* control function priors */

real<lower=0> sigma_xi_sd;

real sigma_p_mean;
real<lower=0> sigma_p_sd;

real gamma_mean;
real<lower=0> gamma_sd;

real lambda2_mean;
real<lower=0> lambda2_sd;

vector[n_categories] mu_lambda_cat;
vector<lower=0>[n_categories] sigma_lambda_cat;

/* Covariates */

/* Different variables will have different covariates selected from
a common set. For simplicity, just copy the data values */

vector[dim_q]          x_q[n_clients, max_transactions];
vector[dim_w]          x_w[n_clients, max_transactions];

real<lower=0>          obs_q[n_clients, max_transactions];
int<lower=0, upper=1>  obs_w[n_clients, max_transactions];

real                   obs_z[n_clients, max_transactions]; /* z_ij */
vector[n_categories]   x_c[n_clients, max_transactions];
/* ^^ This must be in 1-of-k indicator vector. */

}

parameters {
/* Random effects priors */
vector[dim_t]          mu_t;
vector[dim_q]          mu_q;
vector[dim_w]          mu_w;
real                   mu_lambda;

cov_matrix[dim_q]      inv_Sigma_q;
cov_matrix[dim_w]      inv_Sigma_w;
real<lower=0>          sig_lambda;

/* Random effects */

vector[dim_q]          beta_q[n_clients];

real sigma_p;
real gamma;

/* Fixed effect priors */

mu_w  ~ multi_normal_prec(mu_w0, inv_V_w0);

inv_Sigma_t ~ wishart(df_t0, S_t0);
inv_Sigma_q ~ wishart(df_q0, S_q0);
inv_Sigma_w ~ wishart(df_w0, S_w0);
sig_lambda  ~ cauchy(sig_lambda_mean,sig_lambda_sd);

/* Priors for control function */

sigma_p       ~ normal(sigma_p_mean,sigma_p_sd);
gamma         ~ normal(gamma_mean,gamma_sd);

  /* Random effects */

  beta_q[i]  ~ multi_normal_prec(mu_q, inv_Sigma_q);
  beta_w[i]  ~ multi_normal_prec(mu_w, inv_Sigma_w);

  for (j in 1:n_transactions[i]) {
    
    if(j < n_transactions[i]){
      // Add the likelihood term for every observation but the last one
      
      increment_log_prob(log_two_logistic_logpdf(obs_t[i,j], dot_product(x_t[i,j], beta_t[i]), exp(alpha)));
      
      obs_q[i,j] ~ lognormal(dot_product(x_q[i,j], beta_q[i]), exp(sigma));

      // Control function
      // Step 1 - price equation
      obs_p[i,j] ~ lognormal(lambda1[i] + lambda2*obs_z[i,j] + dot_product(x_c[i,j],lambda_categories), sigma_p^2);

      // Step 2 - add correlation terms into the logit utility
      b[i,j] ~ normal(0,1);

  }

               sigma_p_mean  = 0.5, sigma_p_sd  = sqrt(2), # scale parameter

That's a bit much to understand even with the clear explanation of
what you're trying to do.

When you say the model's slow, do you mean each iteration's slow
or that you get low effective sample size per iteration, or both?

To get rid of the warning messages, you can reduce the initial
step size. That tends to help with not jumping into regions that
cause arithmetic issues (like the overflow causing your warning).

One issue may stem from this,

> top <- exp(xb) * t^alpha ;
> bot <- 1 + exp(xb) * t^alpha;
>
> return log(1 - top/bot);

because if top is near bot, this is going to return -inf.

Stan also uses the scale (sd) parameterization of normal and
lognormal, not the variance one.

- Bob

That's a bit much to understand even with the clear explanation of

When you say the model's slow, do you mean each iteration's slow
or that you get low effective sample size per iteration, or both?

To get rid of the warning messages, you can reduce the initial
step size.  That tends to help with not jumping into regions that
cause arithmetic issues (like the overflow causing your warning).

One issue may stem from this,

> top <- exp(xb) * t^alpha ;
> bot <- 1 + exp(xb) * t^alpha;

> return log(1 - top/bot);

Stan also uses the scale (sd) parameterization of normal and

Thank you :)

I have a question about vectorization - 
I am able to vectorize the nested loop that uses ~normal, ~lognormal and ~bernoulli_logit.
However since I am also using increment_log_prob, which the manual says accepts vectors only for compatibility but is not more efficient, looping will still be happening.

So my question is - is looping over increment_log_prob AND the other function slower than only looping over the increment_log_prob? 
Will it speed up things to take vectorize the built in function or is it useless?

Thank you!

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Model running time and a possible issue with lognormal scale parameter
parts:
Vectorize everything you can without changing the log
density.

These two things shouldn't be noticeably different speed-wise:

increment_log_prob(v);

for (i in 1:num_elements(v))
increment_log_prob(v[i]);

The first may be a little bit faster because the second loops twice.

Stan compiles loops very efficiently to C++. So it's not like BUGS or
JAGS or R or Python looping. Where the savings comes in is
if we can reduce the size of the automatic differentiation expression graph or
share computations.

The reason the above two are the same speed is that increment_log_prob
implicitly stores up the values in a list, then vectorizes internally.

- Bob

I realize that using the LKJ transformation instead of inv wishart will make things much better, but I also tried removing the correlation between the betas, as well as a random intercept model with correlated betas, but none of them seems to perform better.

> > > and then pass a positive transformation of sigma to the function:
> > > obs_q[i,j] ~ lognormal(dot_product(x_q[i,j], beta_q[i]), sigma^2);
> > > or
> > > obs_q[i,j] ~ lognormal(dot_product(x_q[i,j], beta_q[i]), exp(sigma));
> > >
> > > In both cases I keep getting these error messages (although only at the beginning but multiple times and definitely not sporadically) .
> > >
> > > Informational Message: The current Metropolis proposal is about to be rejected because of the following issue:
> > > stan::prob::lognormal_log(N4stan5agrad3varE): Scale parameter is inf:0, but must be finite!

> > >
> > > Model code:
> > > functions {
> > >
> > > /* Eq (5) in Zhang 2014 (published) */
> > > real log_two_logistic_logpdf(real t, real xb, real alpha) {
> > > real top;
> > > real bot;
> > >

> > > bot <- 2 * log1p(exp(xb) * t^alpha);
> > >

> > > }
> > > }
> > >
> > >
> > > data {
> > >
> > > /* Dimensionality information */
> > > int<lower=1> n_clients;

> > >
> > > int<lower=1> dim_t;
> > > int<lower=1> dim_q;
> > > int<lower=1> dim_w;
> > >
> > > /* Hyperparameters (priors) */
> > > real sigma_mean;
> > > real<lower=0> sigma_sd;
> > >
> > > real alpha_mean;
> > > real<lower=0> alpha_sd;
> > >
> > > // Prior means
> > > vector[dim_t] mu_t0;
> > > vector[dim_q] mu_q0;
> > > vector[dim_w] mu_w0;
> > > real mu_lambda_mean;
> > >
> > > cov_matrix[dim_t] inv_V_t0;

> > > real<lower=0> mu_lambda_sd;

> > > cov_matrix[dim_q] S_q0;
> > > cov_matrix[dim_w] S_w0;
> > > real<lower=0> sig_lambda_sd;
